content.title: Bond denied for woman accused of shooting SC police chief, prompting Blue Alert
content.text: BARNWELL, S.C. (WIS) - A woman charged with opening fire at a Midlands police chief on Monday will remain behind bars.A judge in Blackville denied bond for 37-year-old Lacey Cushman on Tuesday. Cushman faces multiple charges, including attempted murder, failure to stop for a blue light and assault of a high and aggravated nature.She appeared virtually for her hearing.Lacey Cushman(WIS)Officials later identified Springfield Police Chief Adam Evans as being injured in the shooting, which happened in neighboring Barnwell County. Springfield, a town of less than 500 people, is located in Orangeburg County. Midlands police chief recovering after being shot during incident that sparked Blue Alert(WIS)Evans was at home and off duty when the Orangeburg County Sheriff’s Office called him in to assist with a shots-fired call involving Cushman. Springfield Mayor Trent Still said that Evans got to the scene of the incident before OCSO deputies, but later found Cushman at a place she frequently visits. A chase then ensued, with Evans getting close enough to identify Cushman’s license plate.That’s when authorities said Cushman opened fire, hitting Evans close to his ribs. A large bullet hole was also seen in the passenger-side window of Evans’s patrol vehicle. Midlands police chief recovering after being shot during incident that sparked Blue Alert(Tanner Gilmartin)After the shooting, the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division then put out a Blue Alert in search of Cushman, which is issued when a suspect is at large for harming a police officer. Still said that she was someone known to law enforcement. Cushman was taken into custody just before midnight Tuesday. She’s being held at the Barnwell County Detention Center. Evans, meanwhile, is reportedly home and in stable condition as of Tuesday. He was brought on by Still to serve as chief after the latter was elected mayor last November. Evans is the town’s only police officer. Still said he has asked OCSO and the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division for help with patrolling while Evans is still recovering.At around 10:35 p.m., officials said they were looking for Cushman, who they described a white woman who is 5 feet 9 inches tall and weighs about 200 pounds.Deputies said she was last seen driving a 2011 white Chevrolet Traverse with an S.C. tag, 706IRU, in Barnwell County.This was not the first South Carolina shooting involving an officer on Monday. In Anderson County, a suspect was killed after shooting a deputy during a traffic stop on I-85 on Monday.Feel more informed, prepared, and connected with FOX Carolina.
